audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's level chart is inverted against content's win[] on every one of the 7 rows: phases[].side reads Nami/Nami/Nami/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill for L1,L2,L3,L4-5,L6,firstitem,2+items, while win[] (backed by real whys[]/spikes[] text about Ebb and Flow's net-zero trades and Tidal Wave's engage) reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Nami/Nami/Nami/Sona.
audit.why: The level chart tells a reader Nami wins the lane early and it's even/Sona-favored late, while the paragraph beneath it says the exact opposite — even early, Nami-favored mid-to-first-item, Sona takes over at 2+ items.
audit.corrected: Moved all 7 phases[].side to match win[], with ratings and .why rewritten to state the real interaction (Aqua Prison sidestep window, Ebb and Flow's cost-free poke, Tidal Wave's knockup-into-bubble chain-CC, Sona's late aura/Power Chord uptime).

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.difficulty's flat 'Tricky matchup — difficulty 7/10, Nami threat 7.5/10' line is fine as a summary but the phases above it disagreed with which stages are actually hard, so the difficulty rating had no grounded chart underneath it.
audit.why: Point 2 requires the lane-difficulty narrative to be internally consistent with the level chart it summarizes.
audit.corrected: Chart now agrees: even L1-3, Nami-favored L4-5/L6/first item (the real difficulty), Sona-favored at 2+ items — matches the overall 7/7.5 rating.

audit.why: Level 2 (Aqua Prison + Ebb and Flow chain trade), level 6 (Tidal Wave knockup opens for a bubble-chain kill), first item (Nami's net-zero W poke still edges the sustain war), and 2+ items (Sona's persistent aura DPS and Power Chord slow out-scale her cooldown-gated heal) are the real power spikes and content already states them accurately.

edits.before: Q-chord the contacts — the aura poke is quiet and constant; the lane pays per note.
edits.after: Even: both of you are poke-sustain supports trading auras, and Aqua Prison's slow travel time is dodgeable — neither wins without a misstep.

edits.before: W answers the trades: the sustain mirror opens and yours compounds.
edits.after: Even: Ebb and Flow's bubble-into-heal trade is strong, but your aura damage matches it — don't clump with your carry where one W bounces to both.

edits.before: Full kit: the chord colors decide trades — power chord the carry, speed the disengage.
edits.after: Even: neither support can force a kill without the other missing a skillshot; hold spacing rather than forcing the fight.

edits.before: Aura economy: chip, heal, speed — the margins are invisible and decisive.
edits.after: Ebb and Flow costs her nothing net once it lands both directions — her poke war edges ahead of your aura chip here.

edits.before: Crescendo online — grouped lanes pay the dance tax; your duo's all-in has a stage.
edits.after: Tidal Wave (R) is a wide knockup-and-slow that opens her ADC's all-in — an R into a landed Aqua Prison chains enough CC to delete you or your carry, so hold Crescendo as the answer, not the opener.

edits.before: First item: the auras compound and the chords chunk.
edits.after: Her W poke still costs nothing net, so she edges the sustain war around first item — play the long game rather than trying to out-trade her here.

edits.before: Late Sona scales into a one-button teamfight: crescendo the clump and aura the cleanup.
edits.after: Two items in you overtake her: your persistent aura DPS and Power Chord slow beat her cooldown-gated Ebb and Flow, and your uptime wins extended fights over her burst-poke windows.

edits.before: - Nami Aqua Prison: matchup-defining — The bubble starts every Nami play — sidestep it and her kit is small numbers. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep E Song of Celerity banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: Aqua Prison (Q) has a slow travel speed and is dodgeable with a sidestep — whiff it and her kit is small numbers until it's back. Tidal Wave (R) opens her ADC's all-in; hold your own Crescendo as the answer, not the opener. Song of Celerity banked for the bubble, not chip.
